Ah, it is a great and frightening command. The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to leave the warm and soft bed, to leave the comfortable and peaceful home. Through this command he is cast into a sea of great struggle and great effort. And then this struggle takes place on land, in the seas, in the practical life of human beings, and in the human conscience, everywhere.

Someone who lives only for himself sometimes lives a very pleasant life, but he lives an extremely small and insignificant life and dies like an ordinary person. The great man is the one who takes up great responsibility. Therefore for such a great man it is no longer possible to sleep, comfort is not granted to him, warm beds rarely come to him, and luxury and ease no longer have any connection with him. He no longer has the leisure even to arrange his provisions. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had grasped the reality, so when Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her) was reassuring him and telling him to sleep, he said: "Khadijah... the time of sleep has gone." Yes, that era has passed. Now is the era of wakefulness, the time of being constantly alert. Now there is struggle, or jihad, and long hardships.

Or add to it... and recite the Qur'an distinctly and slowly (4) [73:1–4]: "O you who wrap yourself up, stand (in prayer) through the night, but little of it: half of it, or lessen it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an slowly and distinctly."

Tartil of the Qur'an (recitation slowly and distinctly, with tajwid, i.e., the rules of correct recitation) means reciting the Qur'an according to its principles, neither hastily nor in a manner resembling singing and music.

There are authentic narrations from the Prophet ﷺ that during qiyam al-layl he did not pray more than eleven rak'ahs, but in these eleven rak'ahs he spent slightly less than two-thirds of the night, and he recited the Qur'an very slowly and distinctly with tajwid.

Imam Ahmad narrated in his chain from Yahya ibn Sa'id (this is Ibn Abi 'Arubah), from Qatadah, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Sa'id ibn Hisham, that he came to Ibn 'Abbas and asked him about the witr prayer. He said: "Shall I not tell you about someone who knows the most among all the people of the earth about the witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Go to 'A'ishah and ask her, and then tell me what answer she gives." Sa'id ibn Hisham said: I said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." She said: "Do you not recite the Qur'an?" I said, "I do." She said, "The character of the Messenger of Allah was the Qur'an." I resolved to stand up, then I thought I should ask about the qiyam al-layl of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I said, "O Mother of the Believers, how did the Messenger of Allah perform qiyam al-layl?" She said, "Do you not read Surah al-Muzzammil?" I said, "Yes, I read it." She said: "Allah made qiyam al-layl obligatory in the first part of this surah, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions practised qiyam al-layl for a year, until their feet swelled, and Allah withheld the conclusion of it in the heavens for twelve months. Then in the last part of this surah He revealed the lightening of it, after which qiyam al-layl became voluntary, whereas before it had been obligatory." I resolved again to stand up and leave, but then a thought about the witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to me. I said, "O Mother of the Believers, tell me about the witr of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." She said: "We would prepare his miswak and water for wudu. Allah would wake him at night whenever He wished to wake him. He would first use the miswak, then perform wudu, then pray eight rak'ahs, and he would not sit in them, sitting only after the eighth rak'ah. He would sit and remember Allah, supplicate, then rise without giving the salam, so as to pray a ninth rak'ah. Then he would sit and remember Allah, the One, then supplicate, then give the salam, and we would hear the sound of the salam. After that he would sit and pray two rak'ahs while seated. This makes eleven rak'ahs. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became old and his blessed body became heavy, he would pray the seventh rak'ah as the witr, then after the seventh he would pray two rak'ahs sitting. Thus there are nine rak'ahs." And it was the habit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that when he performed a prayer he liked to be constant in it, and whenever he could not wake up at night, or was prevented by pain or sickness from rising at night, he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day. I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ever completed the whole Qur'an in one night, nor do I know that he ever fasted an entire month except Ramadan." (Imam Muslim also narrated it from Qatadah; see Zad al-Ma'ad of Ibn al-Qayyim for details.)

This training of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was being carried out because a heavy responsibility was about to be placed upon him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verse 5:

"Indeed, We are going to send down upon you a weighty word" (73:5). This refers to this Qur'an, and beyond the Qur'an there are further commands. The Qur'an is not heavy in its wording; it is easy. And taking admonition from it is also very simple. But in the scale of truth it is extremely weighty, its effects are far-reaching, and the responsibilities of establishing this system are heavy.

"Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and broken into pieces out of fear of Allah" (59:12). Therefore Allah sent this Qur'an down upon a heart that was firmer than a mountain, and so it received it.

Then, to receive the light of the Qur'an, to know its reality, and to acquire its comprehension is very heavy, and it requires very long preparation and training. To establish contact with the higher realm, to reach the soul of this universe, and to reach the living and lifeless spirits of this universe, in the way that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attained access to it, is a long and weighty responsibility, and it requires long struggle and training.

Then, to stand firmly upon the straight path of Islam without hesitation and without doubt, not to look to either side, not to be influenced by the inclinations and attractions of the world, to keep crossing the obstacles on this path, and to bear the difficulties that come, is a very heavy responsibility, and it too requires long preparation and striving.

Staying awake at night while people are asleep, being far from the impurities of everyday life, shaking off the worldly entanglements and becoming wholly Allah's, receiving the light and bounties of Allah, becoming intimate with the Absolute Unity and being purified for it, and in the calm and stillness of the night reciting the Qur'an with such measured recitation that it is as though this Qur'an is being revealed right now, and this entire universe is flowing along with the Qur'an. Even apart from human words and expressions, this entire universe is in harmony with the Qur'an. In the Qiyam al-Layl, a person receives the rays of the light of the Qur'an, its indications, in a very tranquil environment, and all of this is the provision for this difficult path. For the difficulties of this harsh path were awaiting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they await everyone who takes up this call. Whoever carries out the work of Islamic call in any age, in the darkest moments of satanic whisperings and of this path, it is this provision that serves a caller, and his path is illuminated by it.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verse 6:**

﴿Indeed, the rising at night is most effective for controlling the self and most suitable for reciting the Qur'an correctly.﴾ It is also more suitable for reciting the Qur'an properly. This refers to rising after the 'Isha' prayer. The meaning of the verse is that rising at night is a hardship for the body, and

﴿and more upright in speech﴾ (Mujahid said: it means more firm in goodness), because after the struggle of the day, fatigue prevails, and a soft bed is very alluring. This is very effective for trampling down the body. But whoever performs this act effectively declares that spirituality dominates him, and that he has answered the call of Allah, and that he is ready to sacrifice everything for that call. For this reason, the Noble Qur'an can also be recited well at night. The remembrance of Allah has sweetness at night, the prayer can be offered with great humility and devotion, and supplication and seeking forgiveness before Allah can be done well at night. Love of Allah is born in a person's heart. The person finds rest, and acquires intimacy and affection, and tranquility, joy and light arise in the heart. This station is not attained in the daytime prayers. Allah, who created this heart, knows its reality well. Allah knows what can affect it, what it is affected by, at which times the heart is most influenced and ready to receive good effects, and what causes have the greatest influence upon it.

Allah was preparing His servant and Messenger for a great struggle, and great duties were about to be revealed to him. Therefore Allah made qiyam al-layl (night prayer) obligatory upon him, because it is the most suitable method for subduing the self. Through it the self is thoroughly trampled, and then it helps greatly in reciting the Qur'an and understanding its wisdom. Furthermore, during the day a person has countless engagements, these engagements take up much time, and human attention remains distracted in various directions, and a large portion of human strength is spent on them.

"For you, during the daytime, there are many occupations" (73:7). Therefore, the day should be passed in those occupations, and the night should be set apart for Allah, occupied with prayer and remembrance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verse 8:

﴿And remember the name of your Lord, and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion.﴾ (73:8)

Remembering the name of Allah does not mean merely that a person keeps repeating Allah's name while counting beads on a rosary of one hundred or one thousand. Rather, the remembrance meant here is that Allah's name is on the tongue and Allah's majesty is present in the heart. Or it may mean that you should perform the prayer, in which there is nothing but the remembrance of Allah and the recitation of the Qur'an. And tabattul (devotion, from the root meaning to cut oneself off) means to cut oneself off from everything other than Allah, to become fully engaged in worship and remembrance, to turn aside from every preoccupation and every thought, and to stand before Allah with one's inner feelings and thoughts.

When tabattul, whose meaning is to cut oneself off from everything except Allah, has been mentioned, it became necessary to make clear that no one else is worthy of this. Allah alone deserves that a person turn towards Him.

Lord of the east and the west; there is no god but He, so take Him alone as your Trustee (73:9). He is the Lord of everyone who turns to Him. He is the Lord of the east and the west, the One God, and there is no god besides Him. Whoever becomes devoted to Allah relies upon Allah, and this belief naturally settles in his mind: that Allah is absolutely Powerful over the east and west of this universe and over the whole universe.

And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to whom it is being said: Arise, for you have taken upon yourself a heavy responsibility in this world. For this, it is necessary that you belong entirely to Allah and, turning your back on the whole universe, turn towards Allah, because strength, power and provision for this task come from that very source.

After this, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is directed towards the attitude his people are adopting towards him: people are turning away, levelling accusations, keeping others away from the right path, and denying. Leave these deniers to Me; I will deal with them, for I have prepared a severe punishment for them, and I will take severe retribution from them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verse 10:

If this narration is correct, that the opening verses of this surah were revealed at the beginning of the prophetic mission, then this second part was certainly revealed somewhat later, at a time when the Messenger ﷺ had begun to proclaim the message openly, and deniers and those who inflicted violence upon the workers of the movement had come into the field, and these people were adopting a harsh attitude towards the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims. And if the other narration is correct, then the first part too was revealed at the time when the polytheists and deniers had begun to taunt the Messenger ﷺ, and these people were active in blocking the path of the Islamic call.

Whatever the case may be, enjoining the night prayer (qiyam al-layl) and remembrance and reflection (dhikr and fikr) together with patience (sabr), (and these two matters are generally found together), is an excellent provision for the Islamic movement. And the difficulties of this path can be borne only through these weapons and measures, because this path is very long and demands patience, whether it is a struggle in the field of human thought or the blows of the battlefield. Both are difficult tasks, and both require patience.

﴿Be patient over what they say﴾ (73:10), because these people used to carry out provocative actions and display an intolerable degree of obstinacy.

﴿And part from them with gracious parting﴾ (73:10). There should be no reproach, nor should you become angry with them; there should be neither boycott nor enmity. This was the plan of the Islamic call throughout the entire Meccan period, especially in the early days of Makkah. Only the heart, conscience, mind and intellect were appealed to. Preaching was to be done with great gentleness, and only the realities were to be explained clearly.

And against their acts of aggression and denial, the defence could only be made through patience of a beautiful kind, along with the remembrance of Allah. Allah has commanded every Messenger to be patient, and has done so repeatedly. Then Allah has also commanded the companions of every Messenger and the believers who came after them to be patient. Even after the eras of the Messengers, whoever has taken up the banner of the Islamic call has had patience as his provision; patience has remained his arms and equipment. Patience is the best shield and the best weapon; patience is the best fortress and refuge. It is a jihad against the self (nafs) and its desires. It is a struggle against the self's deviations and desires. It is also a struggle against the self's rebelliousness, haste and despair. And it is the best defence and weapon against the enemies of the Islamic call, their intrigues and their harms. And generally it is also a weapon against the human self, which usually devises ways to escape the hardships and responsibilities of the Islamic call. The human self, in various colours and garments, wants to escape the responsibilities of this call and does not wish to walk on the straight path. For the caller, there remains no alternative except to be patient over all these matters. Remembrance and patience go together; wherever patience is required, it is possible only with the remembrance of Allah.

And, O Prophet, be patient with beautiful patience over what these people are saying, and leave them in a most gracious manner. Leave to Me those who deny, and I shall take care of them myself.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 73, verse 11:

﴿Leave Me with those who deny, the people of luxury, and give them respite for a little while.﴾ These are the words that have always been spoken by the Almighty, the Compeller, the One of great might. Those who deny are sons of Adam, whereas the One who issues the threat is the One who created them. And the One who created this vast and immense universe created the whole of it with the single word "Be" (kun).

Leave me alone to deal with these deniers; this call is My call, and your responsibility is only to convey it. Let them deny, and you leave them in a dignified manner. I Myself will take up the battle against them. Do not be anxious about this.

Indeed, it will be a catastrophe that crushes them to pieces. When Allah, the Almighty, the Compeller, turns His attention towards them, He will shatter their strength to pieces, and these people, who consider themselves "possessors of blessings," will be reduced to nothing and utterly destroyed.

﴿And give them respite for a little while.﴾ Even if they are granted the respite of the whole life of this world, it is still a short time. In the reckoning of Allah, it is only a part of one day. And even by these people's own estimate, the whole of life is a brief moment. On the Day of Resurrection, they themselves will estimate that they stayed in the world only a day or part of a day. In any case, however long the respite given to the apparent disbelievers may be, it is still short. If Allah's seizure does not come upon them in this world, the Hereafter is very near.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verses 12–13:

﴿Indeed, with Us are heavy shackles and a blazing Fire, and food that chokes in the throat, and a painful punishment.﴾ (73:12–13)

The word "ankal" means shackles. "Jahim" means Hell. "Ta'am dhu ghussa" refers to food that is so choking that it tears the throat. This is a fitting recompense for those who were given blessings, yet showed no regard for them and did not give thanks for them. O Muhammad, be patient, practise patience of the beautiful kind, and leave the matter of dealing with them to Us. We have a great deal of provision for them. First there are great heavy shackles which will be a cause of torment for them; then there is Hell, which will heat them and burn them intensely. Then there is for them food that sticks in the throat and wounds it. And beyond that, there is a severe punishment, and this punishment will be given to them on a terrifying day.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verse 14:

"On the Day when the earth and the mountains will quake, and the mountains will become like heaps of sand, scattered about." This will be on the Day when the earth and the mountains tremble, and the state of the mountains will become like heaps of sand that are being scattered.

This is the terror of that Day; within its reach is this vast earth as well. The earth is trembling and breaking into pieces; these human beings are extremely weak and insignificant. Great spheres will be shattered to bits.

Now the discourse turns toward those people of wealth and blessing, and it is told that Pharaoh was a great tyrant, yet see the end that befell him before you. You have seen the dread of the Resurrection; now also look at this worldly end of Pharaoh.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verses 15–16:

"Indeed, We have sent to you a Messenger as a witness over you, just as We sent a Messenger to Pharaoh. But Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizing." Thus, in brief, a tremor is created within their hearts, and an effort is made to dislodge them from their rigid stance. Before this, the scene of the mountains quaking and being reduced to dust has already passed. The former is the punishment and seizing of the Hereafter, and this is the worldly seizing. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verses 17–18:

"Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day that will make children grey-haired, and by which the sky will be split asunder? His promise is ever fulfilled." This will be so terrifying a state of affairs that the sky will split apart and break into pieces; then the earth too will be split and crushed to powder, and on that day the children who are present will turn grey with grief. This terror now enters into the human self. What will be the condition of living human beings? Even these children will grow old, and people's sense of feeling is turned in this direction. Then, by way of emphasis, it is said that this will surely happen.

"Indeed, His promise is always fulfilled" (73:18): this is an event that will occur, because it is God's will, and events take place according to God's will.

After this horror, which has appeared in the form of the trembling of the earth, the Day of Resurrection, and the fright of the human soul, it is now told what the way of protection from it is.

This is a reminder; so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.

In truth, the path to Allah is very easy, compared with those paths that are doubtful and frightening and terrifying, because it is the straight path.

Here, on one hand, fear and tremor were placed in the hearts of the obstinate deniers of Islam; on the other hand, the blessed heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the weak and few believers were given comfort, so that they might be at ease and be certain that your Lord is with you, and that He Himself will deal with your enemies. For them there is only a short respite, a known time. After that, the matter between truth and falsehood will be decided, and when the time of that decision comes, whether in this world or in the Hereafter, Allah will then take vengeance upon His enemies. He will drown them as He drowned Pharaoh, or He will bind them in chains on the Day of Resurrection and roast them in the punishment of Hell, and it will be a severe punishment. Remember that Allah does not leave His friends without help, and if He gives respite to enemies, He gives it only for a certain time.

Now comes the second part of the surah, and this whole part is in the form of one long verse. According to the narrations, it was revealed one full year after the first part of the surah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 73, verse 20:

Indeed, your Lord ... Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

This is a beautiful concession. It is good news for one burdened, exhausted and worn out: relief has come. It is a fitting lightening and exemption announced by Allah for the Prophet and the believers. Allah knew that they were sincere and that they were carrying out the commands with great devotion. Because of prolonged standing in prayer at night, their feet had swollen, and much of the night was being spent in reciting the Qur'an and in prayer. It was not Allah's purpose that people be put into hardship through the Qur'an; rather, the purpose was to prepare the Prophet and the Muslims for the great responsibility being placed upon them. And since they were to carry out this responsibility throughout their lives, this training was necessary for them.

The manner in which the matter is expressed here is extremely reassuring.

Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you as well (73:20). Allah has seen your standing in prayer by night, and He has seen your companions too. Allah has accepted this worship of yours. Allah knew that your sides and theirs part from warm and soft beds. You did not heed the call of those soft beds, but you heeded the call of Allah. Now Allah shows mercy to you, and grants a degree of lightening to you and your companions.

And Allah measures the night and the day (73:20). That is, sometimes the night is longer and sometimes the day. You and your companions worship for a third of the night, half the night, or two-thirds of the night. Furthermore, Allah knows the limits of your strength, and Allah's purpose is not to exhaust you or to punish you. Allah is preparing you for a purpose. When you have become prepared, then He lightens (the burden); so you too should lighten (the burden) on your own selves, and do not be so strict in this matter now.

So recite of the Qur'an as much as is easy for you (73:20). That is, during the night in prayer. But do not put yourselves into hardship and distress. Here, certain matters are also mentioned in which the Muslims were to be engaged in the future, and along with these duties, standing in prayer at night was somewhat difficult.

He knows that there will be some among you who are ill (73:20). For them, the obligation of standing in prayer at night would be burdensome.

And others who travel through the land seeking the bounty of Allah (73:20). That is, travelling in search of livelihood and the hardships of travel, because the struggle for livelihood is also among the necessities of life. The purpose of Islam is not that you should abandon the struggle for the needs of worldly life and become monks.

And others who fight in the way of Allah (73:20). Allah knew that soon He would permit jihad against oppression, that the banners of Islam would be raised, and that rebels would be confronted. Therefore, for the sake of that confrontation, this lightening is now made. Now recite as much as you can without hardship.

So recite of it as much as is easy for you (73:20). Without hardship and distress. And remain firmly steadfast in the remaining religious obligations.

And establish prayer and give zakat (73:20). And after that, give a goodly loan as well.

And lend to Allah a goodly loan. Whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah; it is better and greater in reward (73:20). And keep turning to Allah in such a way that you continually seek forgiveness, asking pardon for your shortcomings, since humans commit faults and err, even though they strive and endeavour to set things right.

And seek forgiveness from Allah; indeed Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful (73:20). This is a pinch of mercy, compassion and ease, and after a year of night prayer, this facility is now revealed. Allah has lightened (the obligation) for the Muslims. Now night prayer became voluntary, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) nonetheless remained upon his practice. His night prayer never decreased from a third of the night onward. It was a discourse with Allah, in the solitude of the night, far from the noise and tumult of the world. Thus he drew provision for the journey from that intimate communion. This struggle continued throughout his entire life. Yet even in sleep, when his eyes were closed, his heart remained awake; his blessed heart remembered Allah at all times. He was connected with Allah at every moment, whether asleep or awake. In short, he had separated himself from all the defilements of the world and become devoted to his Lord. And in this path, he bore as much burden as he was able to bear.
